title: _topo_order length-mismatch guard is unreachable for cycles/disconnects and emits a misleading empty-set error on the only path that reaches it
description: Inside Pipeline._topo_order the block `if len(sorted_ids) != len(self._nodes): missing = {n.name for n in self._nodes} - set(sorted_ids); raise ValueError(f"Cycle detected or disconnected nodes: {missing}")` is dead/misleading. topo_sort_ids (delegating to graphlib.TopologicalSorter) registers every node via sorter.add(nid) and returns list(sorter.static_order()), which yields ALL added nodes including fully disconnected ones; a genuine cycle raises CycleError inside topo_sort_ids and propagates, never returning a short list. Therefore len(sorted_ids) == len(self._nodes) for every cycle-free graph, and cycles never reach this line at all. The only way to make len(sorted_ids) < len(self._nodes) is duplicate node names (two functions with the same __name__, which _register_node silently allows because it overwrites _node_map but appends both to _nodes). In that case `missing = {names} - set(sorted_ids)` is the EMPTY set (the duplicated name is present in sorted_ids), so the error reads 'Cycle detected or disconnected nodes: set()' — it names neither the real cause (duplicate node name) nor any node. So the branch is unreachable for its stated purpose and actively misleading for the one input that triggers it.
evidence: topo_sort_ids (_topo.py:51-69): `for nid in node_ids: sorter.add(nid)` then `return list(sorter.static_order())`; CycleError is raised before returning. Verified with graphlib: disconnected nodes ['a','b','c','d'] with only a->b yields static_order ['a','c','d','b'] (len 4 == input 4, branch not taken); duplicate ['x','x','y'] yields ['x','y'] (len 2 < 3, branch taken) and {names}-set(sorted) == empty set. test_topo_order_cycle_raises / test_self_loop_detected assert CycleError (from topo_sort_ids), not this ValueError; no test ever exercises line 304.
behavior_preservation: Removing the branch is behaviour-preserving for all currently reachable inputs (cycles still raise CycleError from topo_sort_ids; disconnected nodes are still caught downstream by run()/score()'s 'no inbound edges' guard). Duplicate node names are a distinct latent defect that this branch obscures rather than reports; if desired they should be rejected explicitly at registration with the offending name, not via a set-difference that yields the empty set.
est_reduction: ~4 lines removed; or replace with an explicit duplicate-name guard at registration that actually names the colliding node.
